clue.text: Amid revolution, Thailand once installed old time communist

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so the old letter goes into the reversed country name
a revolution turns something round, so the old name for Thailand is read backwards

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A communist installed in power amid upheaval in old Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: Siam is the old name of Thailand; the surface's 'old time communist' is split, with 'old' and 'time' giving single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Chairman Mao's brand of Marxism is a communist.

clue.text: Animals Scotsman discovered on a Greek island

parts.note: Mac is a crossword name for a Scotsman, from the common surname prefix
Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A Scotsman stumbles on some creatures while holidaying on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Macacos are macaques, a kind of monkey, so they are animals.

clue.text: Sailing vessel going off course in lake? Rot!

indicators.note: a ship going off course strays, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a story of a boat that strayed off course in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Rot!' look like an exclamation of disbelief, but they supply fodder letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanker carrying petroleum is a vessel that sails the seas.

clue.text: Dirty dog briefly kept in enclosure on farm

indicators.note: something kept in an enclosure sits inside it, so the shortened dog goes inside

parts.note: a sty is a pen where pigs are kept

indicators.note: said briefly, a word loses its last letter

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog is kept in a filthy pen on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty dog' reads as one insult, but 'Dirty' is the definition and the dog is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Smutty jokes are dirty, i.e. indecent; smut is also literal grime.

clue.text: Draughts in a country house

definitions.meaning: the board game known in the US as checkers
the British Prime Minister's country retreat

explanation.surface: Someone plays draughts in a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: The board for draughts is chequered, and in Britain the game itself is called chequers; Chequers is also the Prime Minister's official country residence in Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: Canadian French that German tennis player's spoken

parts.note: que is French for that

indicators.note: spoken means the tennis player's name is said, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Boris Becker is the German former Wimbledon champion

explanation.surface: A Canadian speaks French, as the German tennis star does.
explanation.walkthrough: BECKER said aloud gives the sound of the last part, spelt BECER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Quebecer is a native of the Canadian province of Quebec.

clue.text: Artist from Midwestern state

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An artist hailing from a state in the Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Dada and Surrealist painter.

clue.text: Support American in disgrace

indicators.note: in places the American abbreviation within the word for disgrace

parts.note: a stain on one's character is a disgrace

explanation.surface: An American is supported while in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to bear up or uphold, i.e. to support.

clue.text: Officers scowl at Russian soldiers possibly led by commander

indicators.note: led by means the commander's abbreviation comes in front of everything else

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
to lour is to frown or scowl
Serge is a typical Russian man's name (Sergei)
soldier ants are a caste of ant, so ants may be soldiers

explanation.surface: Officers glare at Russian troops under the leadership of their commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian soldiers' looks like one phrase but splits into a name and insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour sergeants are senior non-commissioned officers in British infantry regiments.

clue.text: Thrown out, scholar gets in a state

indicators.note: thrown suggests letters tossed about and landing in a different order

explanation.surface: A scholar is thrown out but finds a new place in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is the link; 'in a' looks like a container but just ends the answer as written, after OUT SCHOLAR rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: South Carolina is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Each tune's different for this singer

indicators.note: different means the letters are made into another arrangement

parts.note: the S of the possessive is kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A singer gives every song her own distinctive treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female singer, especially in a nightclub or cabaret.

clue.text: Bit-part actor given kiss in famous film, by God!

indicators.note: in puts the kiss inside the title of the film

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's celebrated 1982 film
X is the kiss symbol at the end of a letter
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A minor actor gets a kiss in a classic film, astonishingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by God!' reads as an exclamation but supplies the Egyptian god RA.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a performer hired for a non-speaking background role.

clue.text: Writer sounds sarcastic

indicators.note: sounds says the word for sarcastic is to be taken as it is pronounced

parts.note: sarky is informal British for sarcastic

explanation.surface: A writer comes across as sarcastic.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SARKY (British slang for sarcastic) is pronounced like the pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro, the Edwardian short-story writer.

clue.text: Author produces chapter on street fighting

indicators.note: letters fighting are jumbled into disorder

explanation.surface: An author writes a chapter about a street brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was the English writer behind the Father Brown stories.

clue.text: If bitten by dog, I'll look fearful

indicators.note: something bitten by a dog is held within its jaws, so the little word sits inside

parts.note: a terrier is a breed of dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bitten by a dog, someone expects to look frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written from the frightener's point of view: one who makes others look fearful.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifier is something that frightens, making people look afraid.

clue.text: Criminal showing composure and very little resistance, on getting pulled in

indicators.note: getting pulled in means this small word is drawn inside the rest

parts.note: poise is calm composure
R is the symbol for resistance, a single letter being very little

explanation.surface: A criminal stays cool and offers hardly any resistance on being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting pulled in' looks like arrest but puts ON inside POISER.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoner is a criminal who kills or harms with poison.

clue.text: Louis Caron performing in Shakespearian role

indicators.note: performing letters put on a show in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor called Louis Caron plays a part in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriolanus is the title role of Shakespeare's Roman tragedy.

clue.text: Gossip about strip club

indicators.note: about means the gossip word goes around the other

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful gossiping woman
to bare is to strip

explanation.surface: Gossip is going round about a strip club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip club' reads as one phrase; 'strip' is fodder and 'club' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub with floor-show entertainment.

clue.text: German red from Rhine area is rubbish

parts.note: rot is the German word for red

explanation.surface: A German wine from the Rhine is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Grot is British slang for junk or worthless stuff.

clue.text: Occupation of property — half of gite north of French city

indicators.note: north of in a down clue puts this piece above the next
half of takes two of the four letters of the word

parts.note: Nancy is a city in Lorraine, north-east France

explanation.surface: Renting a French holiday cottage north of Nancy.
explanation.walkthrough: GITE (a French holiday cottage) gives its back half, TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the holding of a property as a tenant, i.e. living in it.

clue.text: Damage caused by conflict

definitions.meaning: a graze or scuff on a surface

explanation.surface: Harm resulting from a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a mark of harm on a surface, and also an informal word for a fight or tight spot.

clue.text: Musical family making money

definitions.meaning: the section of instruments such as trumpets and trombones

explanation.surface: A family of musicians who are making a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpets, horns and trombones form one family of orchestral instruments, and in northern English slang the word means cash.

clue.text: A drunkard goes round clubs in town

indicators.note: goes round means the drunkard's word surrounds the card suit letter

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A drunk does the rounds of the nightclubs in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a Berkshire town famous for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a town in Berkshire, England.

clue.text: Look back at fighting against France: that makes sense

indicators.note: against means placed right next to the following piece
back means the word for look is read from right to left

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
F is the international vehicle code for France
action is military combat, i.e. fighting

explanation.surface: A look back at fighting against France makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that makes' links the wordplay to the definition 'sense'.
explanation.definitionFit: Olfaction is the faculty of smell, one of the five senses.

clue.text: Second thoughts about helping to back Tory party

indicators.note: to back means this piece goes at the rear

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Con is short for Conservative
a side is a party in a dispute
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A Tory party member has second thoughts about lending support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping to back' reads as supporting, but sends RATION to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconsideration means thinking a matter over again, i.e. having second thoughts.

clue.text: Class initially unwilling to enter examination

indicators.note: to enter means the first piece goes inside the word for examination

parts.note: a trial is a test or examination

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil, initially reluctant, sits a test in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' does two things in the surface but in the parse it is fodder, with 'enter' its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a small teaching session, i.e. a class.

clue.text: Some kings and queens are soon pursuing power

indicators.note: pursuing means the second piece follows behind

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
early can mean soon, before the expected time

explanation.surface: Royalty are soon chasing power.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London Cockney charity figures in button-covered costumes; the adjective defines them.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes London costermonger royalty who wear suits sewn with mother-of-pearl buttons.
